gloss: to suffer, to be in pain

definitions.gloss: to suffer, to be in pain
definitions.explanation: To experience physical or emotional distress.

examples.japanese: {病気|びょうき}で{苦|くる}しむ。
{苦|くる}しんでいる{人|ひと}を{助|たす}ける。
examples.english: To help people who are suffering.

examples.japanese: {頭痛|ずつう}に{苦|くる}しんでいる。
{借金|しゃっきん}に{苦|くる}しむ。
お{金|かね}に{苦|くる}しむ。
{人手|ひとで}{不足|ぶそく}に{苦|くる}しんでいる{会社|かいしゃ}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many companies are struggling with a labor shortage.

notes:
{苦|くる}しむ means to suffer, struggle, or be in distress—physically or mentally.

TRANSITIVITY:
Intransitive verb (no object taken).

CONJUGATION (godan む-verb):
- {苦|くる}しまない (negative)
- {苦|くる}しみます (polite)
- {苦|くる}しんだ (past)
- {苦|くる}しんで (te-form)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- Xに{苦|くる}しむ: to suffer from X
- Xで{苦|くる}しむ: to suffer due to X
- {病気|びょうき}に{苦|くる}しむ: to suffer from illness
- {借金|しゃっきん}に{苦|くる}しむ: to struggle with debt
- {貧困|ひんこん}に{苦|くる}しむ: to suffer from poverty

RELATED WORDS:
- {苦|くる}しい: painful, difficult, agonizing
- {苦|くる}しみ: suffering, pain, agony (noun)
- {苦労|くろう}する: to have a hard time, struggle
- {悩|なや}む: to worry, be troubled

NUANCE:
{苦|くる}しむ emphasizes ongoing suffering or distress, while {悩|なや}む focuses more on mental worry or concern.
